texts: This is a game of lying, guessing and arguing.
Somewhere in this village, hidden among you, are werewolves.
Everyone else is trying to find them before it's too late.
At the start, everyone gets a secret role card.
Look at it, and never show it to anyone, not even when you die.
If your card is a werewolf, you're on the wolf team.
Almost everyone else is on the village team.
A few special roles play only for themselves.
The game switches between night and day.
At night, everyone closes their eyes and keeps them closed until the moderator says to wake up.
The moderator calls certain roles to wake up, one at a time, and do something secret.
The werewolves wake up together and silently point at someone to kill.
Other roles might protect a player, or secretly check whether someone is on the village team.
If you aren't called, keep your eyes shut and stay quiet.
Tapping on the table helps cover up any sounds.
In the morning, everyone wakes up and finds out who died.
Dead players are out of the game.
They can't talk, hint or make faces.
Then the village argues about who might be a werewolf.
To put someone on trial, one player nominates them and a different player seconds.
Each person on trial gets to defend themselves.
Then the moderator counts three, two, one, vote, and on the word vote, you raise your hand for anyone you want out.
You can vote for more than one person.
If half of the players still alive vote for someone, they're eliminated.
If there's a tie for the most votes, nobody is eliminated.
The village wins when every werewolf is dead.
The werewolves win when there are as many of them as everyone else.
Some special roles have their own way to win.
Werewolves, your job is to lie, blend in and point fingers.
Villagers, listen closely, ask questions and watch for anyone acting strange.
You all live in a quiet little village.
But lately, every morning, someone turns up dead.
The village has figured it out: some of you are werewolves.
By day they look like everybody else.
Your job is to figure out who they are before they get everyone.
Or, if you're a werewolf, to make sure nobody figures out it's you.
The village team is the biggest.
Plain Villagers are on it, along with special villagers who have powers, like the Seer, who can check people at night, or the Bodyguard, who can protect someone.
It's the werewolves, plus sometimes helpers like the Minion, who knows who the wolves are but isn't one.
They aren't on either team, and each one has their own strange way to win.
At the start, everyone gets a role card.
This is the most important rule of the game: never show your card to anyone.
Not during the game, and not after you die.
You're allowed to lie about what your card says.
But you can never prove it by showing it.
If you forget what your role does, ask the moderator quietly.
They don't play, they don't take sides, and they know everyone's role.
They call the night, tell the story in the morning, and run the vote.
If there's ever an argument about the rules, the moderator decides, and that's final.
When the moderator says night falls, everyone closes their eyes and keeps them closed.
The moderator will call roles one at a time, like, Seer, wake up.
Only that role opens their eyes, does their thing silently by pointing or nodding, and closes their eyes again.
The werewolves wake up together, look at each other so they know their pack, and silently agree on one player to kill.
Everyone else should tap on the table or make a little noise, so nobody can hear who's moving.
The moderator calls every role every night, even roles that are already dead, so you can't learn anything from what gets called.
Here are a few common roles.
The Seer wakes up and points at a player.
The moderator gives a thumbs up if that player is on the village team, and a thumbs down if they aren't.
The Bodyguard picks one player to protect from being killed that night.
The Witch has two potions, one that saves the werewolves' victim and one that poisons someone, and each can be used only once.
The Hunter, when they die, gets to take one last shot and eliminate another player.
Cupid picks two players to be Lovers, and if one Lover dies, the other dies of a broken heart.
At the end of this tutorial, you'll hear exactly which roles are in today's game.
When night is over, the moderator says, everyone wake up.
Then they tell the story of what happened, and who didn't survive.
Sometimes nobody dies, because someone was protected.
You stay at the table, but you can't talk, hint or make faces for the rest of the game.
Depending on how we're playing, the moderator might also announce the dead player's role.
This is the heart of the game.
You can claim a role, like, I'm the Seer, and last night I checked Alex.
But remember, anyone can lie, and the werewolves definitely will.
A werewolf might claim to be the Seer too.
When two people claim the same role, at least one of them is lying.
When you're ready to accuse someone, say, I nominate, and their name.
Someone else has to second it.
A nomination with no second doesn't count.
Once players are on trial, each of them gets a turn to defend themselves, in the order they were nominated.
While they defend, only they may talk.
If the moderator says someone has been silenced, they have to defend themselves without saying a word, using only gestures.
After the defenses, the moderator names each player on trial and counts down, three, two, one, vote.
On the word vote, raise your hand if you want that player out.
If two people tie for the most votes, nobody is eliminated.
And if nobody gets enough votes, nobody goes.
Then night falls again, and the cycle repeats.
The village wins when every werewolf is dead, along with any other threats in the game.
The werewolves win when there are as many of them as everyone else, because at that point they control every vote.
Loners and special roles have their own goals, and the moderator will tell you about any that are in play.
Some winners share the victory with their team, even if they died along the way.
So don't give up when you're dead.
Your team can still win for you.
Pay attention to how people vote, not just what they say.
Werewolves often protect each other, or pile onto someone innocent.
Watch for anyone who's too quiet, or too eager to push a vote.
If you have a power, think before you reveal it.
The wolves will come after you the moment they know.
And don't be afraid to change your mind when new information comes out.
Act exactly like you would as a villager.
Don't all defend each other, that's a giveaway.
Sometimes it even helps to vote against a fellow wolf who's already doomed.
That's called busing, and it makes you look innocent.
At night, think about who's most dangerous to you, like whoever seems to have good information.
Stay calm and keep your story straight.
A few rules to keep the game fun.
Don't talk when your eyes are supposed to be closed.
No swearing on your life, or making promises outside the game to prove your role.
Lying is part of the game, so don't take it personally, and nothing that happens in the game carries over after it ends.
And most of all, have fun.
Close your eyes when night falls, open them when it's day, argue like your life depends on it, and vote wisely.

What is the Patton Token? The Patton Token (FM3) is our name for the Ivory Tower. The first player eliminated in a game gets it, and in the next game they can't be the first one eliminated. The app passes it on when a new game starts and reminds you on Night 1 and Day 1.
Should I call roles that are dead? Yes. Keep calling every role each night and pause as if they're acting. Otherwise players learn which roles are gone.
Can dead players talk? No. Dead players stay silent.
Can players show their cards? Normally no. Players may claim anything out loud, but cards stay hidden until they die (or the Prince / Village Idiot reveal).

What does the Seer see? Your group's rule: thumbs up if the player's card is on the village team, thumbs down if it isn't. That means werewolves, the Minion, the Sorceress, Vampires and loners like the Tanner all get thumbs down. Two cards are built to fool the Seer: the Lycan (village) gets thumbs down and the Wolf Man (wolf) gets thumbs up. Lovers are read by their own card.

How do the Lovers win? Lovers on the same team win with that team, even if other players are still alive. Lovers on different teams win together only as the last two alive. If one Lover dies, the other dies of heartbreak.
When do the werewolves win? When the werewolves equal or outnumber all other living players. The Minion and Sorceress don't count as werewolves for this.
When does the village win? When every werewolf (and any Vampire) is dead.
Does the Bodyguard stop the Witch's poison? Standard play: the Bodyguard only stops the werewolf attack. Decide as a house rule if you want otherwise.
What is the balance score? Each role has a weight in the spirit of Ultimate Werewolf's point system (approximate). Positive helps the village, negative helps the wolves. Aim close to 0.
Villager. Village. No special power. Talk, read people, and vote out the werewolves.

Seer. Village. Each night, points at one player. Thumbs up if that player's card is on the village team. Thumbs down if it isn't (werewolves, Minion, Sorceress, Vampires, loners). House rule: the Seer reads each player's actual card team. Two cards are built to fool the Seer: the Lycan gets thumbs down and the Wolf Man gets thumbs up. Lovers read by their own card, not by being a Lover.

Bodyguard. Village. Each night, chooses one player to protect. That player can't be killed that night by anything: werewolves, vampires, poison, the Huntress, the Chupacabra or the Revealer. House rule: protection covers every night kill, not just the werewolves. Newer editions: can't protect themselves or the same player two nights in a row (the app warns you).

Witch. Village. Has one healing potion and one poison potion, each usable once per game. The healing potion protects that player from every night kill that night, not just the werewolves. Wakes after the werewolves and is shown who they chose.
Hunter. Village. When eliminated, takes one player down with them. The app prompts you for the Hunter's shot whenever they die.

Cupid. Village. On the first night, links two players as Lovers. If one Lover dies, the other dies of heartbreak. Lovers on the same team win with that team. They don't need to be the last two alive. Lovers on different teams win together only as the last two alive. If one Lover dies, the other dies of heartbreak.
Mason. Village. Masons wake on the first night to see each other. Usually dealt as a pair. Anyone who talks about the Masons out loud is eliminated that night (Ultimate Edition rule).
Apprentice Seer. Village. Becomes the Seer once the Seer is eliminated.
Aura Seer. Village. Each night, learns whether a player has a special role (anything other than plain Villager or Werewolf).
Mentalist. Village. Each night, picks two players and learns whether they are on the same team.
P.I.. Village. Once per game, chooses a player and learns if that player or either neighbor is a werewolf. Neighbors are the living players seated on each side.
Beholder. Village. On the first night, learns who the Seer is.
Insomniac. Village. Each night, learns whether at least one of their neighbors woke up. The app works this out from the roles that woke tonight.
Revealer. Village. Each night, may point at a player. If it's a werewolf, the werewolf dies. If not, the Revealer dies.
Gravedigger. Village. Each night once someone has died, points at a dead player and learns their exact role. Custom role. Best with Full reveal off, since revealed roles make it pointless.

Priest. Village. Once per game, blesses a player. That player survives the next night kill of any kind: werewolves, vampires, poison, the Huntress, the Chupacabra or the Revealer. House rule: the blessing covers every kind of night kill.
Huntress. Village. Once per game, eliminates a player at night.
Old Hag. Village. Each night, chooses a player who must leave the village (no talking or voting) the next day.
Spellcaster. Village. Each night, silences a player for the next day. They can still vote.
Troublemaker. Village. Once per game, makes the next day have two eliminations.

Drunk. Village. Plays as a Villager until the third night, when they learn their real role. Set a card aside for them at the start. On Night 3, tap that card in the Drunk step and the app switches their role at sunrise.
Ghost. Village. Dies on the first night. Each night after, writes one letter as a clue for the village.

Cursed. Village. A villager until the werewolves attack them. Then they become a werewolf instead of dying. The app switches their role for you. With Vampires in play, a Vampire bite turns them into a Vampire.

Lycan. Village. A villager with wolf blood. Plays for the village, but the Seer sees them as a werewolf (thumbs down). The Seer and the P.I. both read the Lycan as a werewolf. That's the point of the card.
Tough Guy. Village. Survives a werewolf attack for one extra day, then dies at sundown, before night falls. House rule. The app announces the death when you tap Begin Night.
Diseased. Village. If the werewolves kill the Diseased, they get sick and can't kill the next night.
Mad Bomber. Village. When eliminated, the living players on either side are eliminated too.
Prince. Village. If voted out, reveals their card and survives. Werewolves can still kill the Prince at night.

Village Idiot. Village. Must always vote yes to eliminate, on every vote. Count their vote even if they forget to raise a hand. This is the Ultimate Werewolf version. Only the Prince survives being voted out.
Mayor. Village. Their vote counts twice. The vote counter adds the Mayor's extra vote to the total.
Pacifist. Village. Must always vote against eliminating anyone.
Martyr. Village. May step in and die in place of a player the village votes out. The app reminds you during the vote while the Martyr is alive.
Werewolf. Wolf team. Wakes each night with the other werewolves to choose one player to eliminate. Werewolves win when they equal or outnumber everyone else.
Wolf Cub. Wolf team. A werewolf. If the Wolf Cub dies, the werewolves eliminate two players the next night.
Dire Wolf. Wolf team. A werewolf who picks a companion on the first night. If the companion dies, the Dire Wolf dies too.
Dream Wolf. Wolf team. A werewolf who doesn't wake with the pack until another werewolf has died.

Wolf Man. Wolf team. A werewolf who looks like a villager to anyone who checks for wolves. The Seer gets a thumbs up. Wakes and kills with the werewolves and wins with them. The Seer and the P.I. read the Wolf Man as a villager.
Lone Wolf. Wolf team. Wakes with the werewolves, but wins only if they are the last werewolf standing.
Minion. Wolf team. Knows who the werewolves are, but they don't know the Minion. Wins with the wolves. On the wolf team, so the Seer gets thumbs down.
Sorceress. Wolf team. Wins with the werewolves. Each night, looks for the Seer. On the wolf team, so the Seer gets thumbs down. The werewolves don't know who she is.
Tanner. Own team. Hates the job. Wins if they die in any way (voted out, killed at night, shot, anything), and then everyone else loses.

Vampire. Own team. Vampires are their own team. They wake each night to bite a victim and can't be killed by werewolves. The victim dies the next day, the moment the first nomination is seconded. Vampires win when they equal or outnumber everyone else and the werewolves are gone.

Chupacabra. Own team. Each night, picks a player. If it's a werewolf, they die. Once no werewolves remain, anyone it picks dies. Wins if it's the last one standing. The village can't win while the Chupacabra is alive.
Cult Leader. Own team. Each night, recruits one player into the cult. Wins if everyone alive is in the cult. Recruited players keep their own role and team as well.
Hoodlum. Own team. On the first night, marks two players. Wins at the end if both are dead and the Hoodlum is alive. Doesn't end the game. Wins alongside whoever wins.
Illuminati. Own team. Sees every player's role on the first night. Also wins, alongside whoever wins, if they're one of the last 3 players alive when the game ends.
Doppelgänger. Own team. On the first night, chooses a player. If that player dies, the Doppelgänger secretly takes their role.
